contract: SignalSpeak is a local, projector-readable communication tool. The selected phrase and Speak action lead the page; input source and connection state stay visible. Phrase selection requires one movement; Morse remains experimental. Reference: ANT Neuro hackathon prompt and the existing decoder's UDP JSON contract in the repository.

accessibility.evidence: Controls are semantic buttons with labels and pressed states. Keyboard Tab reached the Phrase board button and produced a visible 3px amber focus outline. Space triggered a movement when focus was outside controls. Status has text in addition to color; reduced-motion CSS disables tile transitions.

responsive.evidence: Rendered at 1366x768, 1280x720, and 390x844. No horizontal overflow was observed at 390px or 1280px. The laptop layout keeps the message, phrase board, source badge, and signal panel visible; mobile stacks the signal panel beneath the board.

loading.evidence: Selecting Live EEG or Replay shows a waiting state and local bridge address while the WebSocket connects.

empty.evidence: Before selection, the message box says to choose a phrase; Morse mode says decoded text will appear there.

error.evidence: Stopping packets for 3 seconds changes the replay badge to OFFLINE, shows a decoder/LSL recovery hint, and keeps the selected phrase visible.

partial.evidence: Manual events omit confidence and latency; the panel displays Not provided and a dash rather than fabricated values.

success.evidence: A manual movement selected a phrase, paused scanning, enabled Speak, and offered Undo and Clear. Browser speech status reported completion.

permission.reason: The app uses local input and browser speech synthesis without requesting an access permission.

renderedEvidence.observation: Selected phrase and confirmation controls are prominent; source label and phrase board are visible.
Message, controls, and first phrase tiles fit without horizontal clipping; remaining content scrolls vertically.
